Subject: OpalFin discovery: performance targets, model fit, and deployment options

Thanks again for taking time today — appreciate the clear run-through of how OpalFin is planning to fold ML into payments reconciliation. This note captures what we heard, assumptions, and next steps so everyone has the same view.

Key pain points you called out
- High-cost per-transaction latency spikes during reconciliation windows (current P95 ~450ms, intermittent timeouts at scale).
- Variable payload size: short instructions + long account histories (avg tokens/request ~750, peak ~2,200).
- Strict PII handling and audit trails required for regulator reviews.

Primary goals
1) Hit P95 latency <= 120ms for short-turn requests (<=512 tokens) for the hot-path.
2) Support sustained throughput of ~1,000 reqs/sec during batch windows with burst to 2,500 for 10–15 minutes.
3) End-to-end traceability + customer-managed key encryption for sensitive payloads.

Model / quality constraints discussed
- Using an open model baseline (you mentioned preference for 70B family for accuracy) with aggressive quantized variants for cost reduction.
- We recommend a two-tier approach: a compact quantized 30–40B variant for the hot-path and a higher-capacity 70B variant for long-context/complex reconciliation.

Deployment topology options we discussed
- Hosted Redwood (fastest path): P95 baseline with prefix KV cache and request routing by SLAs. Good for initial pilot; simpler procurement.
- Dedicated pool (reserved capacity): predictable throughput for your batch windows; can pin quantized 70B variants and enforce VPC peering.
- Private (on-prem/VPC): likely required if OpalFin audit requires full control + HSM integration.

Technical notes / risks
- Long-context KV cache: we'll need session sharding to keep memory footprint bounded; this affects batching efficiency for long requests.
- Tokenization variance: peaks at 2,200 tokens will require memory headroom; recommend a 25% headroom buffer in cluster sizing.
- Fallbacks: plan for automatic fallback to smaller model variant on saturation to prevent timeouts.

Attachments: opalfin_perf_targets.xlsx (your perf targets), redwood_sizing_matrix.xlsx (draft sizing matrix).

Proposed immediate next steps
1) Redwood to provide a sizing matrix and cost estimate for (a) Hosted pilot, (b) Dedicated monthly commit, and (c) Private deployment with HSM integration — deliver by Thu 10/14. (Action: Karthik + Marissa)
2) Security questionnaire kickoff: OpalFin to share the baseline SOC2 scope doc; Redwood to map controls (Action: Irene).
3) Schedule a 60m technical deep-dive to align on model variants, quantization approach, and KV cache sharding — propose Tue 10/19 or Wed 10/20. (Action: Sean / OpalFin engineering)

If I missed anything or misinterpreted a target, flag it and I'll update the plan.

Thanks,
Sean

Thanks for the confirmation, Anil. Quick technical clarifications and an initial topology sketch before the call on 10/20: 

Short answers to your questions
1) Prefix/KV cache is stored per-session and can be shared across variants if the architecture keeps a common serialization format. In practice we recommend keeping cache compatibility between your hot-path variant and the larger variant to avoid cache cold starts during fallback.
2) Ballpark cost: quantized 30–40B in a Dedicated pool is roughly 30–45% of the 70B full-precision cost; final pricing depends on commit level and region. We will include a modeled cost table in the sizing matrix.

Topology sketch (high level)
- Ingress layer: API gateway with weighted routing by route key (short-turn vs long-context).
- Hot-path service: quantized 30–40B on Dedicated GPU pool with aggressive batching and prefix caching. Autoscale policy tuned for 1k sustained, burst to 2.5k.
- Deep-path service: 70B variant pinned to separate Dedicated pool with larger memory instances for long sequences.
- Fallback policy: synchronous fallback to deep-path or asynchronous queued processing (depending on SLA).
- Security: TLS everywhere, VPC peering for Dedicated, KMS/HSM for Private. Audit logs forwarded to your SIEM via S3 + CloudTrail mapping.

Sizing notes to validate on the call
- Token headroom for 2,200 token peaks -> reserve ~30% memory buffer per replica.
- Batch latency vs throughput trade-off for hot-path: goal is sub-120ms P95; we anticipate batching window <=12ms for most requests to meet that target.
- KV cache sharding: suggest 256 shards initially; can reduce if we observe low active-session cardinality.

Action items (who/when)
- Karthik / Marissa: finalize sizing matrix and modeled cost table by Thu 10/14.
- Irene: prepare control mapping for SOC2 + HSM integration notes by Wed 10/15.
- OpalFin: share SOC2 scope and existing audit artifacts by Wed 10/14 if possible.

I'll attach a draft sizing matrix (redwood_sizing_matrix.xlsx) — see the Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tabs for the modeled runs.

Karthik
